literal: Than those who live deceiving like those who have renounced, while not renouncing in their mind, hard-hearted people there are none.
translation: There are no people more hard-hearted than those who, without renouncing worldly desires in their minds, live deceiving others by posing as true ascetics.
modern: மனதால் பற்றுகளைத் துறக்காமல், துறந்தவர்களைப் போல நடித்துப் பிறரை ஏமாற்றி வாழ்பவர்களை விடக் கொடிய நெஞ்சமுடையவர்கள் வேறு யாரும் இல்லை.
explanation: This couplet addresses the severe hypocrisy of false ascetics. The phrase 'நெஞ்சின் துறவார்' refers to those who still harbor worldly desires in their hearts, while 'துறந்தார்போல்' describes their outward pretense of having renounced everything. The poet emphasizes that there are no individuals more ruthless or hard-hearted ('வன்கணார் இல்') than these pretenders, as they weaponize a sacred way of life solely to deceive others for personal gain.
